subject: Phase 100366: Full CLI Core Plumbing and Retrieval Read Surface
verdict_justification: The developer successfully delivered the shared argument parser (cli_args), output layer (cli_output), error contract (cli_error), MCP-derived help catalog (cli_help), and the flagship read commands recall, get/show, inspect, and stats routed in-process via McpHandler without drift. Test suite passes (make test exit 0), clippy is clean (make lint exit 0), and workspace coverage is 97.93% lines / 98.90% functions across 286 files with all changed files >=95%. However, five findings were identified: subcommand --help is completely unhandled by read commands, unknown command error reporting ignores explicit --output flags, split_leading_globals misparses consecutive value flags, parse_failure overrides explicit --output formatting, and a minor grammar error in get argument requirements.
standard: requirement.md §4.9.2 (read bindings, tool schema catalog, exit codes)
AGENTS.md file size cap (<=450 lines) and per-file coverage floors (>=90%)
Workspace gates: make test, make lint, make coverage

findings.title: Subcommand `--help` / `-h` is unhandled by the read surface, executing commands or erroring on missing positionals
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_args.rs:118-121 parses `-h` and `--help` into `parsed.flags` under `help`, but `crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read.rs:103-124` never inspects `parsed.has("help")`. Executing `target/debug/clio stats --help --db sqlite::memory:` executes `stats` and returns data payload instead of help text; executing `target/debug/clio recall --help` fails with exit 2 `{"code":"usage","hint":"usage: clio recall QUERY","message":"`recall` requires a QUERY argument","ok":false}`.
findings.requirement_ref: Phase 100366 §1 Expected Outcome, §5 Task 1 & Task 2, AC-100366-01
findings.recommendation: In `cli_read::run_parsed` (or `run_verb`), check `if parsed.has("help")`: render the subcommand usage text and exit with `ExitCode::SUCCESS`.
findings.resolution: Resolved. Added `help_if_requested` in cli_read.rs, called from `run_verb` and `run_with_state` before `McpState::open`, so `clio <verb> --help`/`-h` renders `cli_help::verb_help(verb)` (usage line + bound tool name) to stdout and returns exit 0 without touching the store. Real output: `target/debug/clio recall --help` -> `usage: clio recall QUERY [--bank BANK] [--limit N] [--domains a,b] [--as-of TS] [--time-axis valid|transaction] [--output json|text]` blank line `recall calls the `retrieve` tool.` exit 0; `target/debug/clio stats --help --db sqlite::memory:` -> usage for stats, exit 0; `target/debug/clio get -h` -> usage for get, exit 0. An unknown verb's `--help` still exits 2 as an unknown command. Tests: cli_read_help_tests.rs (all five verbs, both spellings), main_read_tests.rs.

findings.title: Unknown-command error reporting ignores explicit `--output json` on TTY and `--output text` when piped
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/main.rs:94-98 calls `cli_output::report_error(&error, cli_output::stdout_is_tty(), cli_output::no_color_requested())`, where `cli_output.rs:114-119` determines mode strictly by terminal attachment without inspecting `--output`. Live output: on a terminal, `clio recal --output json` outputs colored human text `error: unknown command `recal`` instead of `{ok:false, code, message, hint}`; when piped, `clio recal --output text 2>&1 | cat` outputs the JSON envelope instead of human text.
findings.recommendation: In `main.rs` unknown command handler (or in `cli_output::report_error`), inspect `trailing` or `collected` for `--output json` / `--output text` so an explicit `--output` overrides TTY detection.
findings.resolution: Resolved. Added `cli_output::mode_from_raw(args, is_tty)` which scans raw tokens for the last `--output`/`--output=...` (a value-less `--output` before another flag is ignored); the main.rs unknown-command branch now resolves the mode from `trailing` and passes it to `report_error`. Real output: TTY via `script -qec 'target/debug/clio recal --output json' /dev/null` -> `{"code":"usage","hint":"did you mean `clio recall`?","message":"unknown command `recal`","ok":false}` exit 2; piped `target/debug/clio recal --output text 2>&1 | cat` -> `error: unknown command `recal`` + `hint: did you mean `clio recall`?` exit 2. Defaults unchanged: TTY prints red human text, a pipe prints the JSON envelope. Tests: cli_output_tests.rs (mode_from_raw), main_read_tests.rs.

findings.title: `split_leading_globals` consumes subsequent flag token as value when a leading value flag lacks an argument
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_args.rs:187-195 pushes `args.get(index)` as the flag value without checking `!value.starts_with("--")`. Live output: `target/debug/clio --output --db sqlite::memory: recall q` consumes `--db` as the value of `--output` and treats `sqlite::memory:` as the command verb, exiting 2 with `error: unknown command `sqlite::memory:`` instead of reporting that `--output` requires a value.
findings.recommendation: In `split_leading_globals`, verify that `!value.starts_with("--")` before consuming `value` for a value-taking flag.
findings.resolution: Resolved. `cli_args::split_leading_globals` now appends the following token as a value only when it does not start with `--`, so a value-less leading flag leaves the next flag for the parser. Real output: `target/debug/clio --output --db sqlite::memory: recall q` -> `{"code":"usage","hint":"try `--output VALUE`","message":"flag `--output` requires a value","ok":false}` exit 2 (previously it consumed `--db` and reported `unknown command `sqlite::memory:``). Test: cli_args_tests.rs::split_leading_globals_does_not_consume_a_flag_as_a_value.

findings.title: `parse_failure` in `cli_read` ignores explicit `--output text` when piped and `--output json` on TTY
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read.rs:401-407 hardcodes `mode = if io.is_tty { OutputMode::Text } else { OutputMode::Json };`. Live output: `target/debug/clio recall q --output text --limt 2 2>&1 | cat` outputs JSON `{"code":"usage","hint":"did you mean `--limit`?","message":"unknown flag `--limt`","ok":false}` despite explicit `--output text`.
findings.recommendation: In `parse_failure`, scan `args` for valid `--output json` / `--output text` (or `--output=...`) before defaulting to TTY mode.
findings.resolution: Resolved. Removed the TTY-only `parse_failure`; `run_verb`/`run_with_state` now resolve a parse error's mode with `cli_output::mode_from_raw` over the raw args, so an explicit `--output` wins even though parsing failed. Real output: `target/debug/clio recall q --output text --limt 2 2>&1 | cat` -> `error: unknown flag `--limt`` + `hint: did you mean `--limit`?` exit 2; `--output json` on a TTY prints the envelope (asserted in cli_read_help_tests.rs::parse_error_honors_an_explicit_output_flag).

findings.title: Grammar defect in missing positional argument error message
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read.rs:235 formats error as `format!("`{verb}` requires a {label} argument")`. When label is "ID", `target/debug/clio get` produces `message: "`get` requires a ID argument"` with incorrect indefinite article.
findings.recommendation: Adjust phrasing to `format!("`{verb}` requires an {label} argument")` or choose the article dynamically based on vowel start.
findings.resolution: Resolved. `one_positional` now selects the indefinite article with a small `article(label)` helper. Real output: `target/debug/clio get` -> `{"code":"usage","hint":"usage: clio get ID","message":"`get` requires an ID argument","ok":false}` exit 2; `target/debug/clio recall` -> `message: "`recall` requires a QUERY argument"`. Test: cli_read_help_tests.rs::missing_positional_uses_the_correct_article.

plan_1hr: In crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read.rs, check if parsed.has("help") in run_parsed. Render the subcommand usage text and return ExitCode::SUCCESS.
In crates/clio-lib/src/main.rs, check trailing tokens for `--output json` / `--output text` when reporting unknown command errors so explicit --output overrides TTY detection.
In crates/clio-lib/src/cli_args.rs:split_leading_globals, guard args.get(index) with `!value.starts_with("--")` before consuming it as a value for a value-taking flag.
In crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read.rs:parse_failure, inspect args for explicit `--output` flags before falling back to TTY detection.
In crates/clio-lib/src/cli_read.rs:one_positional, update article formatting to "an {label}" where appropriate.
plan_unlimited: Add dedicated unit and integration tests covering subcommand-level `--help` and `-h` across all read subcommands (`recall`, `get`, `show`, `inspect`, `stats`).
Centralize global flag pre-parsing across top-level dispatch so output mode, color, and database resolution behave identically across all CLI commands and error paths.

plan_unlimited.item: centralize global flag pre-parsing across top-level dispatch
plan_unlimited.note: The raw-args explicit-output scan is centralized in cli_output::mode_from_raw and shared by the unknown-command path and the read parse-error path, so --output now behaves identically on both error surfaces. Full pre-parsing of all globals for every top-level command (ops/retention/compose/setup) is out of scope for these findings and would change those commands' documented parsing; deliberately not done to avoid a drive-by refactor.
